text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Vytautas Landsbergis called the coalition agreement between his Homeland Union and the Christian Democrats a new stage in Lithuania's maturing democracy. The coalition has 86 seats in the 141 seat parliament and is ready to form a government after parliament's first sitting on November 25.

- Germany has made a political decision to grant Lithuania a visa-free regime, said a foreign affairs ministry official after his recent visit to Germany. The actual decision is expected no earlier than 1998.

- President Algirdas Brazauskas has not made a final decision whether or not to the Baltic presidents' summit in Riga next week after his officials were reportedly insulted by Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
- A total 14 banks operate in Lithuania at present, the Bank of Lithuania, the central bank, said. 13 licenses for commercial banks have been cancelled since 1994.
- Lithuanian Railways passenger operations suffered an 83 million litas loss during the first nine months of the year.
- Pensions are to rise to above 200 litas in November.
- The Lithuanian, Polish and Ukrainian presidents expressed in a joint statement their worry over developments in Belarus.
- Some 363 million litas will be spent to develop, modernise and maintain the Lithuanian road network next year.
- The Free Market Economy institute calculates that Lithuanians have to pay more than 50 percent of their income if they all their taxes and social charges.
- The boarder police are to buy 150 Land Rovers for 14.4 million litas.
- Archaeologists discovered a well-preserved pagan altar in Vilnius Old Town, believed to date from the 13th century.
- The suspected leader of the criminal world in the second city of Kaunas, Henrikas Daktaras, will go on trial on December 18 although several key witnesses have been murdered.
